answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a stake-backed history: each identity posts collateral, then earns an anchor score from completed jobs that counterparties verify and can challenge with evidence. A kernel of randomly selected auditors checks disputed outcomes, while a meadow of independent agents supplies varied work so one operator cannot cheaply farm endorsements in a closed ring. Sybils remain possible, but each must lock real capital and risk forfeiting it, making fake identities costly rather than free.
